description: Run one structured program/argv command. Manual and auto-approved modes use Runtime policy plus the Anthropic workspace sandbox. User-confirmed dangerous mode runs directly as the current OS user with host filesystem, working-directory, environment, and internet access and no EASY CODE approval prompt. Explicit one-shot shells remain supported.

propertyDescriptions.program: Executable name or workspace-relative executable; absolute host executables require dangerous mode.
propertyDescriptions.args: The structured argument vector passed directly to the program. Never repeat program or its executable basename in args[0]; args starts with the first real argument.
propertyDescriptions.cwd: Workspace-relative existing directory, or an absolute host directory only in dangerous mode.
propertyDescriptions.intent: The purpose of the command, used by Runtime when applying execution policy.
propertyDescriptions.timeoutMs: An optional requested command-phase timeout. Runtime applies the minimum of this request, the configured command limit, and the classified capability limit, then returns all four timeout values including the effective limit.
propertyDescriptions.reason: A concise explanation of why this command is needed for the current task.

guidance: run_command executes one synchronous structured program/argument-vector command under the active Runtime posture. Put the executable only in program; args[0] must be the first real argument, never program again. Prefer existing project scripts. An explicit one-shot shell may be requested with cmd /c, PowerShell -Command, or sh -c; never request an interactive, login, encoded, or detached shell. Never emulate background execution with nohup, disown, shell background &, Start-Job, Start-Process, or cmd start /b. Outside Dangerous full access, Runtime independently classifies, approves, and sandboxes every process. Terminal failures carry a stable failure.kind: parameter for malformed input, policy for a Runtime boundary denial, approval only when required approval is unavailable or rejected, sandbox for enforcement failure, exit for a nonzero process result, timeout for enforced termination, and runtime for internal lifecycle failures. If Runtime classifies the first sandbox_unavailable result as retryable and explicitly requests one bounded retry, retry exactly once and do not block a DAG for that transient failure. If Runtime then reports a turn-scoped sandbox pause, do not retry again; continue non-command work or return a concise pause report so the next turn can retry.
